kusikiliza kifungu kifupi cha hadithi kuhusu maamkuzi na maagano mepesi kikisomwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au katika kifaa cha kidijitali,
kutambua maamkuzi na maagano yaliyotumiwa katika hadithi aliyoisikiliza akishirikiana na wenzake,
kujadili michoro au picha zenye watu wanaoamkuana na wanaoagana akishirikiana na mwenzake,
kuigiza maamkuzi na maagano (k.v. Hujambo? - Sijambo; Hamjambo? - Hatujambo; Habari? - Njema/Nzuri; Kwaheri -
Kwaheri ya kuonana) darasani akishirikiana na mwenzake au katika kikundi kwa kuzingatia umoja, upendo na heshima kwa wenzake,
kueleza wenzake kuhusu maamkuzi na maagano aliyojadili na mzazi au mlezi wake.
key_inquiry_questions: Unatumia maneno gani kuwasalimu na kuwaaga watu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli ya kikundi, kusikiliza na kutoa maoni yake kikamilifu.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kujifunzia maamkuzi na maagano.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapojifunza maamkuzi na maagano yanayotumiwa katika jamii yake.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoigiza maamkuzi na maagano mbalimbali.
sub_strands.values:
Uzalendo: mwanafunzi anapojadili na mzazi au mlezi kuhusu maamkuzi na maagano katika jamii yake.
Amani: mwanafunzi anapoamkuana na wenzake kwa utulivu.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapomwamkua mwalimu, mzazi au mlezi ifaavyo kwa heshima.

skills.name: Tumia maamkuzi na maagano yafaayo na majibu yake
skills.mastery: Chooses the greeting or farewell that fits who is met (a friend, an elder, a group), the time of day and whether arriving or leaving, and gives the right reply (Hujambo? Sijambo; Shikamoo, Marahaba; Hamjambo? Hatujambo), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Greeting at home and in pre-primary comes before the Kiswahili greetings of Grade 1.
Hearing and repeating short words lets the child say the greeting back.

misconceptions.error: Answers a greeting with the same greeting (Hujambo? Hujambo!) instead of its reply.
misconceptions.cause: The child hears the greeting as a sound to echo, as with "Hello" in English; the question-and-answer pair has not been learnt.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Rafiki anakusalimu: "Hujambo?" Unajibu nini?" with "Hujambo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act it as a ball game: the greeting is thrown, the reply is caught; the two words are on two different cards.
misconceptions.feedback: Ukiulizwa "Hujambo?" unajibu "Sijambo," maana yake sina tatizo.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Greets an elder with a peer or Sheng greeting (Mambo! Sasa!) instead of Shikamoo.
misconceptions.cause: Mambo and Sasa are what the child hears most among children and on the street; he has not been taught that an elder is greeted differently.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unamwona babu njiani. Unamsalimu vipi?" with "Mambo babu!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort picture cards of people (babu, rafiki, mwalimu) into two piles: Shikamoo and Hujambo.
misconceptions.feedback: Mzee husalimiwa kwa heshima: Shikamoo babu!
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the elder's reply to the child's greeting the wrong way round (the elder says Shikamoo, or the child says Marahaba).

example.question: Mtoto anamsalimu bibi: "Shikamoo bibi!" Bibi anajibu nini?

misconceptions.cause: Both words are heard together and the child does not yet know which belongs to the young person and which to the elder.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mtoto anamsalimu bibi: "Shikamoo bibi!" Bibi anajibu nini?" with "Shikamoo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Role-play with a hat for the elder: only the one with the hat may say Marahaba.
misconceptions.feedback: Mtoto anasema Shikamoo; mzee anajibu Marahaba.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the greeting of another time of day.
misconceptions.cause: The child learnt one greeting as a set phrase and uses it at every hour.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unamwona mwalimu asubuhi. Unamsalimu vipi?" with "Habari za jioni mwalimu!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: A clock or sun chart: asubuhi, mchana, jioni, usiku; the child moves the arrow and says the greeting for that time.
misconceptions.feedback: Salamu hufuata wakati: Habari za asubuhi mwalimu!
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a greeting when leaving, or a farewell when arriving.

example.question: Unaenda nyumbani baada ya shule. Unamuaga mwalimu vipi?

misconceptions.cause: Greeting and farewell words are learnt on one chart and the child mixes the two columns.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaenda nyumbani baada ya shule. Unamuaga mwalimu vipi?" with "Hujambo mwalimu!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act out a door: walk in and greet, walk out and say goodbye.
misconceptions.feedback: Unapoondoka unaaga: Kwaheri mwalimu!
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Greets a group with the singular greeting (Hujambo?) or answers for a group with Sijambo.

example.question: Mwalimu anaingia darasani na kusema: "Hamjambo wanafunzi?" Darasa linajibu nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child knows one pair only; the plural forms hamjambo/hatujambo follow the person marker (m-, tu-), which has not been noticed.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anaingia darasani na kusema: "Hamjambo wanafunzi?" Darasa linajibu nini?" with "Sijambo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Greet one child, then the whole row; show that the word changes with one or many.
misconceptions.feedback: Watu wengi hujibu "Hatujambo."
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua namna ya kuketi anaposoma (k.v. kutoinama sana, kuketi wima, kutoning’iniza miguu) kutoka kwenye picha, michoro, magazeti, vitabu, vifaa vya kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake,
kufanya mazoezi ya kuketi ipasavyo anaposoma,
kutambua jinsi ya kushika kitabu ipasavyo kwa kutazama picha au michoro kwenye magazeti, chati, mabango, vitabu, vifaa vya kidijitali n.k. akishirikiana na wenzake,
kufanya mazoezi ya kushika kitabu ipasavyo anaposoma,
kuelekeza macho kutoka kushoto hadi kulia na kutoka juu ya ukurasa hadi chini akiongozwa na mwalimu,
kutazama picha mbalimbali zinazotoka kushoto kwenda kulia na juu kwenda chini,
kufanya mazoezi ya kufungua kurasa za kitabu ipasavyo,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kwa kuzingatia namna ifaayo ya kuketi na kushika kitabu.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia mambo gani unaposoma?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kikundi kuonyesha jinsi ya kuketi ifaavyo, kushika kitabu na kuelekeza macho ipasavyo ili kusoma.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kutazama namna ifaayo ya kutekeleza shughuli ya kusoma.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapomshirikisha mzazi au mlezi kuonyesha jinsi ya kusoma ifaavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kusoma katika kikundi.
Amani: mwanafunzi anapoonyesha utulivu akishiriki katika shughuli za kikundi.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anapowapa wenzake nafasi ya kushiriki wakati wa shughuli za kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis:
Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anajitambua anapojifunza namna ya kuketi, kushika kitabu na kuelekeza macho ipasavyo anaposoma.
Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutazama picha au michoro.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya uwezo wa matayarisho ya usomaji mwafaka yaliyoshughulikiwa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language.

skills.name: Keti vizuri, shika kitabu ipasavyo na usome kutoka kushoto kwenda kulia, juu hadi chini
skills.mastery: Sits upright with the book on the desk at a fitting distance, holds it the right way up with the pages flat, and moves his eyes (and finger) from left to right and from the top line to the bottom, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also watches it in class).

prerequisites.reason: Handling a picture book the right way up in pre-primary comes first.
Left-to-right patterns in pre-primary prepare the eyes for reading direction.

misconceptions.error: Starts reading from the right or from the bottom of the page.
misconceptions.cause: Some children have seen other scripts read from the right, or simply start where the picture is.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaanza kusoma ukurasa kutoka wapi?" with "chini upande wa kulia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Put a green dot at the top left of each page: start at the green dot.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunaanza juu, upande wa kushoto.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Holds the book upside down or back to front.

example.question: Kitabu kiko sawa lini?
example.correct_answer: picha na maandishi yakiwa wima, jalada mbele

misconceptions.cause: The child has handled few books and does not check the picture before reading.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kitabu kiko sawa lini?" with "picha zikiwa juu chini" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Before opening, find the front cover and check that the people in the picture stand up.
misconceptions.feedback: Shika kitabu wima: jalada mbele, picha zimesimama.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads lying on the desk with his face almost on the page, or leaning back far from it.

example.question: Mkao upi ni bora unaposoma?
example.wrong_answer: kulala juu ya meza uso karibu na kitabu
example.correct_answer: kuketi wima, kitabu mezani umbali wa mkono

misconceptions.cause: The child is tired or cannot see well; nobody has shown the reading position.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mkao upi ni bora unaposoma?" with "kulala juu ya meza uso karibu na kitabu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show the "elbow distance": the book is as far as from the elbow to the hand. If the child still leans in, tell the parent to check the eyes.
misconceptions.feedback: Keti wima, kitabu kiwe umbali wa kiwiko hadi kiganja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Loses the line and jumps to another line or back to the start.

example.question: Unapomaliza mstari wa kwanza, unaenda wapi?
example.correct_answer: mwanzo wa mstari wa pili, upande wa kushoto

misconceptions.cause: The eye sweep back to the next line is new; without a finger guide the child lands anywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unapomaliza mstari wa kwanza, unaenda wapi?" with "popote ninapoona neno ninalolijua" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Move a finger or a card under the line; at the end, slide back to the left and down one line.
misconceptions.feedback: Mwisho wa mstari, rudi kushoto kwenye mstari unaofuata.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

kutambua jinsi ya kuketi ipasavyo wakati wa kuandika kutoka kwenye picha,
kuketi ipasavyo wakati wa kuandika,

kutambua namna ya kushika kalamu kutoka kwenye picha, michoro, magazeti, vitabu, vifaa vya kidijitali n.k akishirikiana na wenzake,
kushika kalamu na kuidhibiti ipasavyo,
kuwaonyesha wenzake jinsi ya kushika kalamu ipasavyo wakati wa kuandika,

kuwapa wenzake kazi yake waipitie ili waitolee maoni.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni mambo gani unapaswa kuzingatia wakati wa kuandika?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anapowaeleza wenzake kuhusu namna ya kuketi na kushika kalamu na kisha kuwasikiliza wakitoa maoni yao.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kutazama jinsi ya kuketi na kushika kalamu ipasavyo.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na mzazi au mlezi nyumbani kutazama video kuhusu jinsi ya kuketi na kushika kalamu ipasavyo wakati wa kuandika.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za matayarisho ya kuandika na kuheshimu maoni yao.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapobadilishana kazi na wenzake ili wasahihishiane na kutoleana maoni.
Amani: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kwa utulivu kuonyeshana jinsi ya kuketi.

skills.name: Keti vizuri, shika kalamu ipasavyo na uandike kutoka kushoto kwenda kulia
skills.mastery: Sits upright with both feet on the floor and the book straight, holds the pencil between thumb and two fingers without pressing hard, and writes from left to right along the line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also watches it in class).

prerequisites.reason: Holding a crayon and drawing patterns from left to right in pre-primary comes first.
Knowing which way a page goes, from handling books.

misconceptions.error: Grips the pencil in the fist, or with all the fingers wrapped round it.

example.question: Kalamu inashikwa vipi?
example.correct_answer: kwa kidole gumba na vidole viwili

misconceptions.cause: A fist grip is how small children first hold a crayon; the tripod grip has not been taught.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kalamu inashikwa vipi?" with "kwa ngumi nzima" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pinch the pencil with thumb and pointer, rest it on the middle finger; a small rubber band can mark the place.
misconceptions.feedback: Shika kalamu kwa vidole vitatu, si kwa ngumi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes with the head on the desk or the body twisted, the book at an angle.

example.question: Mkao upi ni bora unapoandika?
example.correct_answer: kuketi wima, miguu sakafuni, daftari limenyooka

misconceptions.cause: The child tires quickly and nobody has shown the writing position.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mkao upi ni bora unapoandika?" with "kichwa juu ya meza" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Check four things before writing: back straight, feet down, book straight, free hand holding the page.
misconceptions.feedback: Keti wima na unyooshe daftari kabla ya kuandika.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Starts writing at the right of the line, or writes letters from right to left.
misconceptions.cause: The child starts wherever there is space, or copies the direction of a sibling's writing in another script.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaanza kuandika mstari kutoka wapi?" with "upande wa kulia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: A green start line at the left margin of each line.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunaandika kutoka kushoto kwenda kulia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Presses so hard the pencil breaks or tears the page.

example.question: Unaandika kwa nguvu kiasi gani?
example.wrong_answer: kwa nguvu sana mpaka karatasi ikatike

misconceptions.cause: The child holds the pencil too tight from worry or from the fist grip.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaandika kwa nguvu kiasi gani?" with "kwa nguvu sana mpaka karatasi ikatike" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Write on a sheet with carbon or soft paper below; the mark should not come through.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika kwa upole: kalamu iteleze.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya Mimi na Sisi (Theme 1: Darasani)
learning_experiences: kusikiliza wimbo unaotumia maneno mimi na sisi kutoka kwa mwalimu au kifaa cha kidijitali,
kusoma sentensi fupi zilizoandikwa kwa kutumia maneno mimi na sisi akishirikiana na wenzake,
kujaza mapengo kwa kutumia mimi na sisi,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi wake sentensi alizokamilisha kwa kujaza nafasi akitumia mimi na sisi ili ampe maoni yake.
key_inquiry_questions: Maneno mimi na sisi hutumiwa kwa maana gani katika mawasiliano?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kutoa mifano ya sentensi zenye matumizi ya maneno mimi na sisi.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapoigiza matumizi ya maneno mimi na sisi darasani.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kusikiliza matumizi ya maneno mimi na sisi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoweza kutumia maneno mimi na sisi ifaavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi kuigiza matumizi ya maneno mimi na sisi.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu maoni ya wenzake katika shughuli ya kikundi.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapotumia maneno mimi na sisi katika mawasiliano kwa kutunga sentensi zenye maadili.
sub_strands.pcis:
Afya ya mtu binafsi: mwanafunzi anapojitambua na kutambua wenzake anapotunga sentensi zinazohusisha maneno mimi na sisi.
Elimu ya mazingira: mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi kuhusu suala lengwa.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya nafsi na dhana inayofunzwa katika somo la English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua maneno mimi na sisi katika sentensi alizopewa
kutumia maneno mimi na sisi ipasavyo katika sentensi alizopewa
kufurahia kutumia maneno mimi na sisi katika mawasiliano

skills.name: Tumia mimi na sisi ipasavyo katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Uses mimi for himself and sisi for himself with others, with the matching subject marker (mimi ni-, sisi tu-), answers a question about himself with mimi, and puts -ni- inside the verb for "me" (alinipa), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying simple sentences about himself and his class in pre-primary.
Greeting and answering (Sijambo) already uses the speaker in the verb.

misconceptions.error: The pronoun and the subject marker on the verb do not agree (Wao anacheza).
misconceptions.cause: The child learns the pronoun as a word and the verb as a fixed form; he has not seen that the verb changes with the person.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Sisi ___ (imba) wimbo." with "ninaimba" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Colour the pronoun and the verb's first syllable the same colour: yeye a-, wao wa-, mimi ni-, sisi tu-, wewe u-, nyinyi m-.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendo hufuata nafsi: Wao wanacheza; Yeye anacheza. (tunaimba)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the one-person pronoun for many people, or the reverse.
misconceptions.cause: The child has not linked the pronoun pair to one and many.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mimi na Ali tunacheza. ___ tunacheza." with "Mimi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Point at one child, then at a group, saying the right pronoun each time.
misconceptions.feedback: Mtu mmoja ni yeye; watu wengi ni wao. (Sisi)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Repeats the pronoun of the question in the answer (Wewe unaenda wapi? Wewe ninaenda sokoni.) instead of switching to mimi.
misconceptions.cause: The child copies the words he heard; changing person between speakers is new.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anakuuliza: "Unaitwa nani?" Unajibu:" with "Wewe ni Baraka." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask and answer in pairs with a pointing finger: wewe points out, mimi points to the chest.
misconceptions.feedback: Ukiulizwa kwa "wewe", unajibu kwa "mimi". (Mimi ni Baraka.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the pronoun after the verb instead of the object marker inside it (Mama alimpa mimi for Mama alinipa).
misconceptions.cause: English says "gave me"; the child adds the separate word instead of -ni- inside the verb.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mama alimpa mimi chakula." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show the verb with the object marker coloured: a-li-ni-pa; compare with the wrong form.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunasema "Mama alinipa", si "alimpa mimi". (Mama alinipa chakula.)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua sauti lengwa katika kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno, au kifaa cha kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutumia teknolojia (k.v. papaya) kusikiliza matamshi bora ya sauti lengwa,
kusikiliza mwalimu au mgeni mwalikwa akitamka sauti lengwa,
kutamka sauti pamoja na mwalimu,

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /m/, /a/, /u/, /k/, /t/, /l/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /m/, /a/, /u/, /k/, /t/, /l/ in syllables and words (mama, kaka, tatu), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The vowels a and u are the end of every syllable of this theme (ma, ku, ta).
Hearing and repeating a sound comes before saying it in a syllable.

misconceptions.error: Says /r/ for /l/, so "lala" becomes "rara".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "lala". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /l/, or do not separate it from /r/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "lala". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "rara" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "lala" ina sauti /l/, si /r/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /g/ for /k/, so "kaka" becomes "gaga".
misconceptions.cause: /k/ and /g/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "gaga" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: "kaka" ina sauti /k/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "mama" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "mama" lina silabi zipi?" with "m-a-m-a" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: ma-ma.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/m/ as "em"), so the syllable cannot be built.
misconceptions.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "m" ni ipi?" with "em" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the sound alone, short (/m/), then join it to a vowel: ma, me, mi.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili tunatamka sauti: /m/.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /m/, /a/, /u/, /k/, /t/, /l/?" with "baba" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "kaka" ina sauti lengwa; "baba" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

kusoma hadithi kutoka kwenye kitabu au kifaa cha kidijtali akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuzingatia matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na kiwango kifaacho cha sauti.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni maneno yapi unayojua kusoma?
Je, kwa nini ni muhimu kusoma kwa sauti inayosikika?

Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali anavyotumia kujifunzia.

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /m/, /a/, /u/, /k/, /t/, /l/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /m/, /a/, /u/, /k/, /t/, /l/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 5 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying the sounds m, a, u, k, t, l and their syllables comes before reading them.
Holding the book and reading left to right comes first.

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "kuku" as "guku".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "kuku" linasomwa vipi?" with "guku" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "kuku" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama ana kuku."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama ana kuku."?" with "Mama ... ana ... kuku." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 5 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, kaka yuko?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, kaka yuko?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

outcomes.text: kutambua maumbo ya herufi kubwa
kuandika herufi kubwa ipasavyo kwa kuzingatia maumbo yake
kufurahia kuandika herufi kubwa ipasavyo kwa kuzingatia maumbo yake

skills.name: Andika kwa hati nadhifu ukitumia herufi kubwa ifaavyo
skills.mastery: Writes a passage of about 5 words in neat handwriting: letters well formed and on the line, capitals only at the start of a sentence or name, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Posture and grip come before forming letters.
Lines and curves of pre-primary are the strokes of the letters.

misconceptions.error: Starts a sentence or a name with a small letter.

example.question: Andika kwa usahihi: mama na baba wako nyumbani.

misconceptions.cause: The child copies words, not sentences; the rule that a sentence and a name begin with a capital is not yet used.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika kwa usahihi: mama na baba wako nyumbani." with "mama na baba wako nyumbani." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Circle the first letter of each sentence and each name in a passage in red.
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi na jina la mtu au mahali huanza kwa herufi kubwa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts capital letters in the middle of words (JuMa, Kitabu KiKubwa).
misconceptions.cause: Some capitals (K, M, S) are easier to form than the small letter, so the child uses them anywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "JuMa ANakula" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort letter cards: capital only at the start; the rest small.
misconceptions.feedback: Herufi kubwa iko mwanzoni tu; nyingine ni ndogo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves no space between words (Mamaanapika).
misconceptions.cause: Spoken Kiswahili runs words together; the child writes the stream as he hears it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Mamaanapikachakula." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Put a finger space after every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Acha nafasi ya kidole kati ya neno na neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Turns b and d (or p and q) round: dada written "baba" or "bada".
misconceptions.cause: Mirror letters are common in early writing; the child has not fixed the direction.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno "dada"." with "bada" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Teach d as "c then a tall line"; trace it in sand.
misconceptions.feedback: Herufi d huanza kama c, kisha mstari mrefu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes letters floating above the line or of mixed sizes, so the line goes up and down.

example.question: Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?
example.correct_answer: juu ya mstari, herufi zikiwa na ukubwa sawa

misconceptions.cause: The child writes fast and does not look at the line.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?" with "popote kwenye ukurasa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Trace the line with a finger first; every letter sits on it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila herufi ikae juu ya mstari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Umoja na Wingi wa Majina (Theme 2: Familia)
learning_experiences: kutambua majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake kwa kutazama vitu halisi, picha au vifaa vya kidijitali k.v. vifaa vya nyumbani,
kutaja majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuimba wimbo unaotaja vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma majina ya vitu katika umoja na wingi akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuandika majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi akishirikiana na wenzake,

Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia majina ya vitu vinavyopatikana katika mazingira yake.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutaja majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi.

Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika vikundi kutaja majina ya vitu kwenye mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuheshimu maoni yao.

kuandika majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi

skills.name: Taja na uandike majina ya vitu katika umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Names and writes things and people of his surroundings in singular and plural by their ngeli (mtoto - watoto, kiti - viti), keeping n-n nouns the same (kalamu - kalamu), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Naming things and people in Kiswahili comes before changing them to the plural.
Hearing the first syllable (ki-, vi-, m-, wa-) of a word.

misconceptions.error: Makes the plural with the prefix of another noun class (kitabu -> watabu).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows that wa- makes people plural and uses it for everything; the ngeli of the noun is not yet known.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "kiti" ni?" with "witi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort noun cards into ngeli families (m-wa, ki-vi, li-ma, n-n) and say each plural aloud.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila ngeli ina wingi wake: kitabu - vitabu, mtoto - watoto. (viti)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Shows the plural only with a number word and leaves the noun singular (kitabu mbili).
misconceptions.cause: English and some first languages keep the noun and add a number; Kiswahili changes the noun and the number agrees.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "mtoto mmoja" ni?" with "mtoto wawili" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Line up two books: the child says vitabu viwili; then three: vitabu vitatu.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino hubadilika pia: vitabu viwili. (watoto wawili)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).
misconceptions.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi ni umoja?" with "vikombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (kikombe)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
misconceptions.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "kalamu" ni?" with "makalamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
misconceptions.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (kalamu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Maneno ya Adabu na Heshima (Theme 3: Tarakimu)
learning_experiences: kutambua maneno ya heshima (asante, pole, tafadhali) kutoka kwenye chati, kadi maneno, mti maneno, kitabu n.k akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutazama michoro mbalimbali na kujadili neno linalofaa kutumiwa katika shughuli husika (k.v. mtu akipokea zawadi, mtu akitaka kupishwa apite) akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusikiliza mazungumzo (k.v. kutoka kwa wanafunzi wenzake, kifungu katika kifaa cha kidijitali) kisha kutambua maneno ya adabu na heshima yaliyotumika,
kuigiza mazungumzo mafupi yanayotumia maneno ya heshima wakiwa na wenzake,
kuzungumza na mzazi au mlezi huku wakitumia maneno ya heshima yanayotumiwa katika jamii na kuambatanisha na hisia zifaazo.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, tunaweza kuonyesha heshima na adabu kwa wenzetu kwa kufanya nini?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana kikamilifu na wenzake katika kikundi kujadili matumizi ya maneno ya adabu na heshima.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunza matumizi ya maneno ya adabu na heshima.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapozungumza na mzazi au mlezi kwa kutumia maneno ya adabu na heshima kutoka katika jamii yake.
Uraia: mwanafunzi anapojua kutumia maneno ya adabu na heshima ipasavyo ili kuimarisha mahusiano katika jamii.
sub_strands.values:
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali ambavyo anatumia kujifunzia maneno ya adabu na heshima.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapotumia maneno ya heshima na adabu katika mawasiliano ya kawaida.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anapotangamana na wenzake bila kuzozana katika shughuli za kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis: Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapotumia maneno ya adabu kuonyesha heshima kwa wenzake na jamii.

outcomes.text: kutambua maneno ya adabu na heshima yanayotumiwa katika jamii
kutumia ipasavyo maneno ya adabu na heshima katika mawasiliano
kuthamini matumizi ya maneno ya adabu na heshima katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Tumia maneno ya heshima na adabu: tafadhali, asante, samahani, pole, karibu
skills.mastery: Picks and uses the polite word that fits the situation (tafadhali or naomba to ask, asante to thank, karibu to answer asante, samahani to apologise, pole to sympathise) and addresses an adult with a title, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Greeting comes before the other polite words.
Polite talk at home in pre-primary.

misconceptions.error: Says samahani when someone else is hurt by accident, where pole (sympathy) is meant.

example.question: Rafiki ameanguka mwenyewe uwanjani. Unamwambia nini?

misconceptions.cause: English "sorry" covers both apology and sympathy; Kiswahili separates them: samahani when I did wrong, pole when you suffer.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Rafiki ameanguka mwenyewe uwanjani. Unamwambia nini?" with "Samahani" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Two pictures: I stepped on your foot (samahani); you fell by yourself (pole). The child names each.
misconceptions.feedback: Pole ni ya kumhurumia aliyeumia; samahani ni ya kuomba msamaha ukikosea.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers "Asante" with "Asante" instead of "Karibu" (or "Si neno").

example.question: Ulimpa rafiki kalamu, akasema "Asante." Unajibu nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child echoes the polite word he has just heard.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ulimpa rafiki kalamu, akasema "Asante." Unajibu nini?" with "Asante" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Practise the pair with two children: one gives, one thanks, the giver answers Karibu.
misconceptions.feedback: Ukishukuriwa, unajibu "Karibu."
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Asks with a bare command (Nipe maji!) without tafadhali or naomba.

example.question: Unataka maji kutoka kwa mama. Unasemaje?

misconceptions.cause: At home and in play the child hears short commands and copies them to adults.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unataka maji kutoka kwa mama. Unasemaje?" with "Nipe maji!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say both versions; the child says which one makes mama want to help.
misconceptions.feedback: Ombi la adabu lina "tafadhali" au "naomba."
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Calls an adult by the bare first name without a title (Mwalimu, Mama, Baba, Bi., Bw.).

example.question: Unamwita mwalimu wako, Bi. Akinyi. Unasemaje?

misconceptions.cause: Children call each other by name and carry the habit to adults.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unamwita mwalimu wako, Bi. Akinyi. Unasemaje?" with "Akinyi, njoo!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Make title cards (Mwalimu, Mama, Babu, Daktari); the child puts one before each name.
misconceptions.feedback: Mtu mzima huitwa kwa heshima: Mwalimu, Mama, Babu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers "Pole" with "Pole" instead of "Asante".
misconceptions.cause: The child echoes the word, as with greetings.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Rafiki anakuambia "Pole kwa kuumia." Unajibu?" with "Pole" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act it: one child is hurt, the other says pole, the hurt one says asante.
misconceptions.feedback: Ukiambiwa "pole" unashukuru: "Asante."
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusoma kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu chenye maneno 6-12 kuhusu suala lengwa na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa (k.v moja, mbili, tatu, nne, tano, sita, saba, nano, tisa, kumi) akishirikiana na wenzake,
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akiwa na wenzake,
kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu alichokisoma,
kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano,
kumweleza mzazi au mlezi kuhusu tarakimu alizojifunza.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unajua hadithi kuhusu nini?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi na kuchangia kikamilifu kuhesabu nambari moja hadi kumi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kutazama na kusikiliza wimbo kuhusu tarakimu.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuhesabu nambari kuanzia moja hadi kumi.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kuhesabu tarakimu na kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowapa wenzake nafasi ya kutoa maoni yao katika kikundi wanapojadili ujumbe katika kifungu.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano.
sub_strands.pcis: Elimu ya pesa: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa.
sub_strands.links:

Somo la Mathematics Activities pia linazungumzia dhana ya tarakimu.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya ufahamu ili kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a very short passage on tarakimu and says what it is about, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it and says the message, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Reading the words of a short passage comes before saying what it means.
Saying who and what about a story heard in pre-primary.

misconceptions.error: Reads every word aloud but cannot say what the passage was about.
misconceptions.cause: All the child's effort goes into sounding out the words; nobody has asked him what the sentences said.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Umesoma kifungu. Kinahusu nini?" with "Sijui, nilikuwa nikisoma maneno tu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: After each sentence stop and ask "Sentensi hii imesema nini?" before reading on.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma tena polepole na ufikirie maana: Kifungu kinahusu kuku wa Juma.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives "watano" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Juma ana kuku watano. Kuku wawili ni weupe. Kuku watatu ni weusi. Juma anawapenda kuku wake." Neno "watano" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Juma ana kuku watano. Kuku wawili ni weupe. Kuku watatu ni weusi. Juma anawapenda kuku wake." Neno "watano" lina maana gani?" with "watoto" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "watano" ni idadi ya tano.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Juma ana kuku watano na anawapenda.

misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Kuku wawili ni weupe." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Juma ana kuku watano na anawapenda.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Juma ana kuku wangapi?" with "Sisi tuna kuku kumi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: watano
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua maumbo ya herufi ndogo kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidijitali,
kushirikiana na wenzake kutambua herufi ndogo kwenye kitabu, chati au chombo cha kidjitali,
kuandika herufi ndogo ipasavyo kitabuni au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali,
kushirikiana na wenzake kutambua maumbo ya herufi ndogo kwenye chati, kitabuni, au chombo cha kidjitali,
kushiriki kuimba nyimbo kuhusu herufi ndogo,
kumwonyesha mzazi au mlezi herufi alizoandika ili azitolee maoni.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unazingatia nini ili kuandika kwa hati nadhifu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kutambua herufi ndogo kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidjitali.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapoandika herufi ndogo akitumia kifaa cha kidijitali.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia herufi ndogo kuandika katika mazingira tofauti na darasa.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuandika herufi ndogo ipasavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi huku akiheshimu maoni yao.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapoandika herufi ndogo ipasavyo kitabuni au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali.
Amani: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kwa utulivu kutambua herufi ndogo kwenye kitabu, chati au chombo cha kidjitali.
sub_strands.pcis: Mtazamo wa ukuaji wa binadamu: mwanafunzi anapojitahidi kuandika herufi kubwa kwa kuzingatia maumbo yake, ukakamavu wake unajengeka.
sub_strands.links:
