Somo la Mathematics Activities pia linazungumzia dhana ya tarakimu.

outcomes.text: kutambua maumbo ya herufi ndogo katika maandishi
kuandika herufi ndogo kwa kuzingatia maumbo yake
kufurahia kuandika herufi ndogo ipasavyo ili kuimarisha mawasiliano

skills.name: Andika kwa hati nadhifu ukitumia herufi ndogo ifaavyo
skills.mastery: Writes a passage of about 5 words in neat handwriting: letters well formed and on the line, small letters of the right height, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Posture and grip come before forming letters.
The capitals of Theme 2 show the shape families of the letters.

misconceptions.error: Writes the tall small letters (b, d, h, k, l) short, so h looks like n.

example.question: Andika neno "habari". Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not use the lines of the book: tall letters must reach the top line.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno "habari". Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "nabari" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Write on three-line paper; the child colours the part of h that goes up.
misconceptions.feedback: Herufi h, k, l, b, d hupanda juu ya mstari wa kati.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes some small letters as big as capitals (kiti written kiTi or KITI).

example.question: Ni neno lipi limeandikwa kwa herufi ndogo vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Capitals were learnt first in pre-primary and feel safer to write.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi limeandikwa kwa herufi ndogo vizuri?" with "KITI" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Compare k/K, s/S, t/T on cards; the child picks the small one for the middle of a word.
misconceptions.feedback: Ndani ya neno tumia herufi ndogo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves no space between words (Mamaanapika).
misconceptions.cause: Spoken Kiswahili runs words together; the child writes the stream as he hears it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Mamaanapikachakula." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Put a finger space after every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Acha nafasi ya kidole kati ya neno na neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Turns b and d (or p and q) round: dada written "baba" or "bada".
misconceptions.cause: Mirror letters are common in early writing; the child has not fixed the direction.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno "dada"." with "bada" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Teach d as "c then a tall line"; trace it in sand.
misconceptions.feedback: Herufi d huanza kama c, kisha mstari mrefu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes letters floating above the line or of mixed sizes, so the line goes up and down.

example.question: Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?
example.correct_answer: juu ya mstari, herufi zikiwa na ukubwa sawa

misconceptions.cause: The child writes fast and does not look at the line.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?" with "popote kwenye ukurasa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Trace the line with a finger first; every letter sits on it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila herufi ikae juu ya mstari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya Huyu na Hawa (Theme 3: Tarakimu)
learning_experiences: kutambua matumizi ya huyu na hawa katika picha,
akiwa kwenye kikundi kutumia huyu na hawa k.v. Mwanafunzi huyu - wanafunzi hawa,
kutunga sentensi zinazojumuisha matumizi ya huyu na hawa,
kusoma sentensi zinazojumuisha matumizi ya huyu na hawa,
kumtungia mwenzake sentensi kwa kutumia huyu na hawa katika kikundi,
kujaza nafasi katika daftari kwa kutumia huyu na hawa.
key_inquiry_questions: Maneno huyu na hawa hutumikaje katika mawasiliano?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kikundi na kuchangia kikamilifu kutunga sentensi akitumia huyu na hawa.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia tarakilishi kuburura majibu sahihi na kuyatia kapuni.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutumia huyu na hawa ipasavyo katika sentensi.
Maadili:
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kufanya zoezi huku akizingatia utunzaji unaofaa.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi kutumia huyu na hawa.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapowatungia wenzake katika kikundi sentensi zenye maadili kwa kutumia huyu na hawa.
sub_strands.pcis: Uongozi na utawala mwema: mwanafunzi anapowaongoza wenzake kutunga sentensi katika kikundi.
sub_strands.links:
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha matumizi ya huyu na hawa na matumizi ya vipashio vya kisarufi katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.
Somo la Mathematics Activities pia linazungumzia dhana ya tarakimu.
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: values: not in the design.

outcomes.text: kutambua matumizi ya huyu na hawa kutokana na picha
kutumia huyu na hawa ipasavyo katika mazungumzo
kuchangamkia matumizi ya huyu na hawa katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Tumia huyu na hawa ipasavyo kutokana na picha
skills.mastery: Points at one person or animal near him with huyu and at many with hawa, and does not use huyu or hii for things, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Telling one from many (Theme 2) comes before the pointing word for each.
Pointing at people in a picture.

misconceptions.error: Uses the people word (huyu, yule) for a thing (kiti huyu).
misconceptions.cause: Huyu was the first pointing word learnt; the child uses it for anything.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kiti ___ ni changu." with "huyu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Point at a child (huyu) and at a chair (hiki); then sort pictures by the pointing word they take.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitu cha ngeli ya ki-vi huonyeshwa kwa hiki; mtu huonyeshwa kwa huyu. (hiki)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the one-thing pointing word with a plural noun (watoto huyu).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun but not the pointing word.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Watoto ___ ni wanafunzi." with "huyu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair the forms on cards: huyu-hawa, yule-wale, hiki-hivi, hili-haya.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto ni wengi: watoto hawa. (hawa)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses hii for every noun (kitabu hii, mtoto hii), as in town Kiswahili.
misconceptions.cause: Hii is the pointing word heard most in town speech, where the noun class is dropped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Mtoto ___ ni dada yangu." with "hii" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read pairs aloud: kitabu hiki, mtoto huyu, nyumba hii; the child hears the match.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitabu hiki; mtoto huyu; nyumba hii. (huyu)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).

example.question: Ni lipi ni la mtu mmoja?

misconceptions.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi ni la mtu mmoja?" with "hawa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (huyu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matamshi Bora Sauti: (/n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/) (Theme 4: Siku za wiki)
learning_experiences: Mwanafunzi aelekezwe:
kutambua sauti lengwa katika kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno au kifaa cha kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutumia teknolojia (k.v. papaya) kusikiliza matamshi bora ya sauti lengwa,
kusikiliza mwalimu au mgeni mwalikwa akitamka sauti lengwa akiwa na wenzake,
kutamka sauti pamoja na mwalimu,
kutamka sauti lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusikiliza silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kidijitali k.v. kinasasauti na rununu kisha kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusikiliza maneno yenye sauti lengwa yakisomwa na mwalimu kisha kutamka maneno hayo,
kumtamkia mzazi au mlezi sauti alizojifunza.
key_inquiry_questions: Ni sauti zipi unazojua kutamka vizuri?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kutambua na kutamka sauti lengwa.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunza matamshi bora ya sauti lengwa.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutamka sauti lengwa na silabi ipasavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kujifunza matamshi ya sauti lengwa, silabi na maneno ya sauti lengwa.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutamkiana na kurekebishana matamshi ya sauti lengwa.
Haki za kijamii: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu matamshi ya wenzake kutoka jamii mbalimbali.
sub_strands.pcis: Mahusiano ya kijamii: mwanafunzi anapotamka maaneno yenye sauti lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya matamshi bora katika Kiswahili na yale yanayofanywa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua sauti lengwa katika matini
kutamka sauti lengwa ipasavyo ili kuimarisha mazungumzo
kutamka silabi za sauti lengwa ipasavyo
kutamka ipasavyo maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa
kuchangamkia nafasi ya matamshi bora katika mawasiliano

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/ in syllables and words (nane, wewe, hii), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Building syllables from m, a, u, k, t, l (Theme 2) comes before the next sounds.
The vowels o, e and i are new targets here.

misconceptions.error: Says /i/ for /e/, so "wewe" becomes "wiwi".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "wewe". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /e/, or do not separate it from /i/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "wewe". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "wiwi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "wewe" ina sauti /e/, si /i/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /u/ for /o/, so "nono" becomes "nunu".
misconceptions.cause: /o/ and /u/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "nunu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: "nono" ina sauti /o/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "nane" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "nane" lina silabi zipi?" with "n-a-n-e" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: na-ne.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/e/ as "ii"), so the syllable cannot be built.
misconceptions.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "e" ni ipi?" with "ii" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the sound alone, short (/e/), then join it to a vowel: ea, ee, ei.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili tunatamka sauti: /e/.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/?" with "mama" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "wewe" ina sauti lengwa; "mama" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Kusoma kwa Ufasaha (Theme 4: Siku za wiki)
learning_experiences: kutambua sauti lengwa (/n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/) katika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akiwa peke yake na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 15 kwa dakika na kwa kuizingatia viakifishi) akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma hadithi kutoka kwenye kitabu au kifaa cha kidijtali akishirikiana na wenzake, akizingatia matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na kiwango kifaacho cha sauti,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa akizingatia matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na kiwango kifaacho cha sauti ili amtolee maoni.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unaweza kusoma silabi zipi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli za kikundi kutambua sauti lengwa.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kusoma kifungu.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu chepesi kwa kuzingatia sauti lengwa.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoweza kusoma kwa ufasaha.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wengine katika matumizi ya vifaa vya kidijitali darasani.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapotunza vifaa vya kidijitali anavyotumia kujifunzia.
Amani: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana kwa utulivu na wenzake kusoma na kuheshimu maoni ya wenzake kuhusu usomaji wake.
sub_strands.pcis: Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anapowapa wenzake nafasi ya kusoma kifungu hadi wamalize wakiwemo wale wasiosoma kwa kasi.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya sauti na vile inavyofanywa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua sauti lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha hadithi
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kiwango kifaacho cha sauti
kusoma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo
kuchangamkia kusoma kwa ufasaha ili kufanikisha mawasiliano

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 15 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying n, o, w, e, i, h comes before reading them.
Reading aloud with the first sounds (Theme 2).

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "wewe" as "wiwi".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "wewe" linasomwa vipi?" with "wiwi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "wewe" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Leo ni siku ya Jumanne."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Leo ni siku ya Jumanne."?" with "Leo ... ni ... siku ... ya ... Jumanne." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 15 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, wewe uko nyumbani?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, wewe uko nyumbani?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kuonyesha nafasi baina ya herufi zinazounda maneno kwenye kitabu, chati au chombo cha kidijitali,
kushirikiana na wenzake katika vikundi kutambua nafasi baina ya herufi katika maneno,
kuandika daftarini maneno kwa kuunganisha silabi akizingatia nafasi ifaayo baina ya herufi zinazounda maneno.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, kwa nini tunafaa kuandika kwa hati nadhifu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki kikamilifu katika shughuli za kikundi kutambua nafasi baina ya herufi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuandika maneno kwa kuzingatia nafasi ifaayo baina ya herufi kwa kutumia kifaa cha kidijitali.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kutambua nafasi baina ya herufi katika maneno.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuheshimu maoni yao.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kufanya shughuli ya kikundi kwa pamoja.
sub_strands.pcis: Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapowathamini wenzake wanaposhirikiana katika shughuli za kikundi.
sub_strands.links:
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha kuandika hati nadhifu na vile inavyofanywa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.
Somo la Mathematics Activities pia linazungumzia dhana ya tarakimu.

outcomes.text: kutambua nafasi baina ya herufi katika maneno
kuandika maneno kwa kuunganisha silabi
kufurahia kuandika maneno kwa kuzingatia nafasi ifaayo baina ya herufi

skills.name: Andika maneno kwa kuunganisha silabi bila nafasi kati ya herufi
skills.mastery: Writes a word by joining its syllables (ma + ma = mama), with the letters of the word close together and no gap inside it, in the right order of syllables, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also checks it in the exercise book).

prerequisites.reason: Forming the small letters comes before joining them into words.
Hearing the syllables of a word lets the child write them in order.

misconceptions.error: Leaves a gap between every letter of a word (m a m a).
misconceptions.cause: The child learnt each letter alone and keeps a space after it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "m a m a" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Write the syllable as one block (ma), then put two blocks together (mama), close.
misconceptions.feedback: Herufi za neno moja hukaa karibu: mama.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins the syllables in the wrong order (ta + tu written tuta for tatu).
misconceptions.cause: The child hears both syllables but writes the one he remembers best first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unganisha silabi: ta + tu" with "tuta" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word and write one syllable per clap, in order, saying each.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika silabi kwa mpangilio unaozisikia: ta-tu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves out the vowel of a syllable (mm for mama, kk for kaka).
misconceptions.cause: The child writes the consonants he hears most strongly; the vowel ending each syllable is missed.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unganisha silabi: ka + ka" with "kk" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Every syllable ends in a vowel: say the vowel long (kaaa) and write it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi huishia kwa irabu: ka-ka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes each syllable on a new line, or one above the other.
misconceptions.cause: Syllable cards were stacked in class and the child copies the stack.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "baba" liandikwe vipi?" with "ba juu, ba chini" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Lay the syllable cards side by side on the desk before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Silabi za neno moja hukaa kwenye mstari mmoja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Umoja na Wingi wa Majina (Theme 4: Siku za wiki)
learning_experiences: kutambua majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake ya darasani kwa kutazama vitu halisi, picha au vifaa vya kidijitali,
kuimba wimbo unaotaja vitu katika mazingira yake,
kusoma majina ya vitu vinavyopatikana katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi,
kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi,
kumzungumzia mzazi au mlezi wake kuhusu vitu katika mazingira ya nyumbani kwa kutumia majina yafaayo katika umoja na wingi.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni vitu gani vya darasani unavyoweza kutaja katika umoja na wingi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi na kuchangia kikamilifu kutambua vitu katika mazingira yake.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapojitahidi kujua majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia majina ya vitu katika umoja na wingi.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi kutumia umoja na wingi.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapotumia umoja na wingi katika mawasiliano kwa kutunga sentensi zenye maadili.
sub_strands.pcis: Elimu ya mazingira na tabia nchi: mwanafunzi anapotaja vitu katika mazingira yake kwa umoja na wingi.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya sarufi katika kiswahili na inavyofanywa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi
kutumia majina ya vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi
kuchangamkia kuzungumzia vitu katika mazingira yake katika umoja na wingi

skills.name: Tumia majina ya ngeli za m-mi na li-ma katika umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Uses nouns of the m-mi and li-ma classes in singular and plural (mti - miti, yai - mayai, jicho - macho) when talking about his surroundings, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The m-wa and ki-vi plurals of Theme 2 come first.
Naming trees, fruit and body parts.

misconceptions.error: Makes the plural with the prefix of another noun class (kitabu -> watabu).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows that wa- makes people plural and uses it for everything; the ngeli of the noun is not yet known.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "mti" ni?" with "viti" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort noun cards into ngeli families (m-wa, ki-vi, li-ma, n-n) and say each plural aloud.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila ngeli ina wingi wake: kitabu - vitabu, mtoto - watoto. (miti)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
misconceptions.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "jicho" ni?" with "majicho" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
misconceptions.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (macho)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Shows the plural only with a number word and leaves the noun singular (kitabu mbili).
misconceptions.cause: English and some first languages keep the noun and add a number; Kiswahili changes the noun and the number agrees.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "yai moja" ni?" with "yai mbili" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Line up two books: the child says vitabu viwili; then three: vitabu vitatu.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino hubadilika pia: vitabu viwili. (mayai mawili)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).
misconceptions.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi ni umoja?" with "majani" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (jani)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Ufahamu wa Kusikiliza Kifungu (Theme 5: Mimi na wenzangu)
learning_experiences: Kusikiliza kifungu cha maneno kati ya 15-20 kikisomwa na mwalimu au kupitia vifaa vya kiteknolojia
kushirikiana na wengine kujadili picha zilizojumuishwa kwenye hadithi,
kutabiri kitakachotokea kwenye hadithi,
kuthibitisha utabiri wake baada ya kusikiliza hadithi,
kutunga sentensi akitumia msamiati uliotumika kwenye hadithi,
kujibu maswali kutokana na kifungu,
kujadiliana kuhusu hadithi waliyosomewa katika kikundi.
key_inquiry_questions: Unatarajiwa kufanya nini unaposomewa hadithi?
Unawezaje kupata ujumbe katika kifungu cha hadithi unachosome wa?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kujadili picha katika hadithi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali katika ujifunzaji.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposikiliza kifungu kikisomwa.
Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapofikiria maana ya msamiati na kuutumia katika sentensi.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowaheshimu wenzake wanaposhirikiana kusikiliza na kujadiliana.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anapowashirikisha wengine katika matumizi ya vifaa vya kidijitali darasani.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapojibidiisha kusikiliza kifungu na kujibu maswali.
sub_strands.pcis: Mahusiano ya kijamii: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kujadili picha kwenye kifungu.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha ufahamu wa kusikiliza na ule unaofunzwa katika somo la English Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa katika kifungu
kutunga sentensi sahihi akitumia msamiati uliotumiwa
kusikiliza kifungu anachosomewa cha maneno kati ya 15-20 na kupata ujumbe
kujibu maswali kuhusu hadithi aliyosikiliza
kuchangamkia kusikiliza kifungu ili kujenga ari ya kusoma

skills.name: Sikiliza kifungu, eleza ujumbe na msamiati wake, na usimulie upya
skills.mastery: After hearing a short passage (Otieno alishiriki chakula chake na Kamau aliyesahau chakula), says its message, gives the meaning of a new word from it, uses the word in a sentence of his own and retells the events in order, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying who and what after a story in pre-primary comes first.
Knowing everyday words lets the child follow the passage.

misconceptions.error: Gives a detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?

misconceptions.cause: The detail is the clearest thing the child remembers; he has not been asked what the passage teaches.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?" with "Kamau alisahau chakula." among the options.
misconceptions.help: After listening, ask "Kifungu kinatufundisha nini?" and compare it with "Nini kilitokea?".
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tushiriki tulicho nacho na wenzetu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives "kushiriki" the meaning of a word that sounds like it.

example.question: Neno "kushiriki" katika kifungu lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the sound of the word to one he knows instead of listening to the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "kushiriki" katika kifungu lina maana gani?" with "kushinda" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Replay the sentence; the child tries each meaning in it and keeps the one that makes sense.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "kushiriki" ni kugawana kitu na mwenzako.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes a "sentence" that only repeats the word and shows no meaning (kushiriki ni kushiriki).

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "kushiriki"?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks any sentence with the word in it is enough.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "kushiriki"?" with "Kushiriki ni kushiriki." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: if your friend did not know the word, would your sentence tell him what it means?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi nzuri inaonyesha maana ya neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells the events out of order.

example.question: Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea.
example.wrong_answer: Walikula pamoja, Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia
example.correct_answer: Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia, walikula pamoja

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers the most exciting event and tells it first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea." with "Walikula pamoja, Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Three picture cards of the events; the child lays them left to right and retells with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
misconceptions.feedback: Matukio yalifuatana hivi: Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia, walikula pamoja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Adds events that were not in the passage when retelling.

example.question: Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?

misconceptions.cause: Retelling is taken as storytelling: the child invents to make it longer.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?" with "ndiyo, ili hadithi iwe tamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: After the retelling, the class checks each event: was it in the passage? Thumbs up or down.
misconceptions.feedback: Kusimulia upya ni kusema yaliyokuwa kwenye kifungu tu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Kusoma kwa Ufahamu Kifungu (Theme 5: Mimi na wenzangu)
learning_experiences: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa (k.v. mimi, wenzangu) kutoka kwenye kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno, kapu maneno akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 13- 16 kuhusu suala lengwa na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akishirikiana na wenzake,
kumweleza mzazi au mlezi kuhusu ujumbe aliopata kutokana na kifungu alichosoma.
key_inquiry_questions: Ni mambo gani unayoweza kujifunza katika hadithi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuchangia kikamilifu katika shughuli za kikundi kutambua ujumbe katika kifungu.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kujifunzia.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapomshirikisha mzazi au mlezi wake kusoma ufahamu kuhusu suala lengwa na kueleza ujumbe.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anapotangamana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi kujadili picha na ujumbe katika kifungu.
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kusoma kifungu.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu na kumweleza mzazi au mlezi ujumbe aliopata.
sub_strands.pcis: Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu kuhusu suala lengwa.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha kusoma kwa ufahamu katika somo hili na ule unaofunzwa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya ufahamu ili kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a very short passage on mimi na wenzangu and says what it is about, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it and says the message, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The vocabulary and message questions of Theme 3 come first.
Reading the words of the passage.

misconceptions.error: Reads every word aloud but cannot say what the passage was about.

example.question: Umesoma kifungu. Kinahusu nini?
example.correct_answer: Kifungu kinahusu Akinyi na rafiki yake Wanjiku.

misconceptions.cause: All the child's effort goes into sounding out the words; nobody has asked him what the sentences said.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Umesoma kifungu. Kinahusu nini?" with "Sijui, nilikuwa nikisoma maneno tu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: After each sentence stop and ask "Sentensi hii imesema nini?" before reading on.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma tena polepole na ufikirie maana: Kifungu kinahusu Akinyi na rafiki yake Wanjiku.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives "tunasaidiana" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Mimi ni Akinyi. Nina rafiki anayeitwa Wanjiku. Tunacheza pamoja shuleni. Tunasaidiana kila siku." Neno "tunasaidiana" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Mimi ni Akinyi. Nina rafiki anayeitwa Wanjiku. Tunacheza pamoja shuleni. Tunasaidiana kila siku." Neno "tunasaidiana" lina maana gani?" with "tunasalimiana" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "tunasaidiana" ni kila mmoja anamsaidia mwenzake.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.
misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Akinyi yuko shuleni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Marafiki hucheza pamoja na kusaidiana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Rafiki wa Akinyi anaitwa nani?" with "Rafiki yangu ni Otieno." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: Wanjiku
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya Kikomo (Theme 5: Mimi na wenzangu)
learning_experiences: kutambua alama ya kikomo (.) katika sentensi kitabuni, kwenye chati au kifaa cha kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuandika sentensi daftarini au kutumia kifaa cha kidijitali kisha aweke alama ya kikomo,
kutumia alama ya kikomo ipasavyo mwishoni mwa sentensi akishirikiana na wenzake,
kumwonyesha mzazi au mlezi alama ya kikomo na kuitumia ipasavyo katika sentensi.
key_inquiry_questions: Alama gani zinazotumika katika kuandika sentensi?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kutambua alama ya kikomo na kuitumia katika sentensi.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapotambua alama ya kikomo katika maandishi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoweza kutumia alama ya kikomo ipasavyo kuandika sentensi.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi na kuheshimu maoni yao.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowatambua na kuwathamini wenzake wakati wa kushiriki katika shughuli za kuandika katika kikundi.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis: Kujitambua: mwanafunzi anapotumia alama ya kikomo kwa usahihi na kuwaonyesha wenzake.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha matumizi ya alama ya kikomo na jinsi inavyotumika katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua alama ya kikomo katika maandishi
kuandika alama ya kikomo ifaavyo katika daftari
kutumia ipasavyo alama ya kikomo katika sentensi
kufurahia kutumia alama ya kikomo ipasavyo katika sentensi

skills.name: Tumia kikomo na herufi kubwa ipasavyo katika maandishi
skills.mastery: Tells a question from a statement, ends each with its mark (? or .), starts the next sentence with a capital, and writes a passage of about 5 words with the marks in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Writing whole words comes before ending a sentence.
The capital that starts the sentence the kikomo ends.

misconceptions.error: Runs sentences together with no kikomo.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Juma alienda shuleni alisoma vizuri alirudi nyumbani
example.correct_answer: Juma alienda shuleni. Alisoma vizuri. Alirudi nyumbani.

misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he speaks, one long breath.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Juma alienda shuleni alisoma vizuri alirudi nyumbani" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the writing aloud; where the breath stops, put a kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila sentensi huishia kwa kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a kikomo at the end of every line of writing, not at the end of the sentence.

example.question: Kikomo huwekwa wapi?
example.wrong_answer: mwishoni mwa kila mstari wa daftari

misconceptions.cause: The line of the book looks like the end of a sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kikomo huwekwa wapi?" with "mwishoni mwa kila mstari wa daftari" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Write one sentence that runs over two lines; the child finds where it really ends.
misconceptions.feedback: Kikomo huwekwa sentensi inapoisha, si mstari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a small letter after a kikomo or kiulizi.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not link the mark to the capital that follows it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mimi ni Amina. mama alifurahi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Every kikomo is a gate: the next word starts big.
misconceptions.feedback: Baada ya kikomo, herufi kubwa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Ends a question with a kikomo.
misconceptions.cause: The child ends every sentence the same way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Unaenda wapi" with "Unaenda wapi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the sentence aloud: if the voice rises and asks, it takes a kiulizi.
misconceptions.feedback: Swali huishia kwa kiulizi (?).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya -angu na -etu (Theme 5: Mimi na wenzangu)
learning_experiences: kutambua matumizi ya -angu na - etu kwa kurejelea vitu katika mazingira yake,
kuigiza matumizi ya -angu na -etu akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi kwa kutumia vitu anavyomiliki k.v. kitabu changu – vitabu vyetu; rafiki yangu - marafiki zetu,
kusoma sentensi zinazotumia maneno - angu na -etu,
kukamilisha sentensi zenye matumizi ya -angu na -etu,
kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia -angu na -etu.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni maneno gani unayotumia kuonyesha kuwa kitu ni chako au ni chenu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi kujadili matumizi ya -angu na -etu.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapotumia -angu na -etu katika mawasiliano.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoigiza matumizi ya -angu na -etu.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kuigiza matumizi ya -angu na -etu.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu maoni ya wenzake wakati wa shughuli za kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapoigiza matumizi ya -angu na -etu akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis:
Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anaposoma sentensi kuhusu suala lengwa.
Mahusiano ya kijamii: mwanafunzi anapowasiliana na wenzake kwa ufasaha akitumia -angu na -etu.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha matumizi dhana ya -angu na -etu na vipashio vya kisarufi vinavyofunzwa katika masomo ya English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua matumizi ya -angu na -etu katika miktadha mbalimbali
kutumia -angu na - etu katika mazungumzo kwa ufasaha ili kuimarisha mawasiliano
kufurahia kutumia - angu na -etu katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Tumia -angu na -etu ipasavyo
skills.mastery: Uses -angu for what is his own and -etu for what he shares with others, with the prefix of the thing owned (kitabu changu, vitabu vyangu, darasa letu), after the noun, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Mimi and sisi (Theme 1) are the owners of -angu and -etu.
The ngeli of the thing owned sets the prefix.

misconceptions.error: Uses the wrong noun-class form of the possessive (kitabu yangu for kitabu changu).
misconceptions.cause: Town Kiswahili uses yangu, yako, yake for every noun; the child has not seen the ngeli agreement.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kitabu ___ (-angu) ni kipya." with "yangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair nouns and possessives by colour: kitabu changu, kiti chake, mtoto wangu.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitabu changu; kiti chake: kimilikishi hufuata ngeli. (changu)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the possessive singular with a plural noun (vitabu changu).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun and forgets the possessive.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Vitabu ___ (-angu) ni vipya." with "changu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change one object to many in front of the child; both words change.
misconceptions.feedback: Vitabu vyangu: vyote viwili hubadilika. (vyangu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the possessive of the wrong owner (-ake for something that is his own, -ake for many owners).

example.question: Mimi na wenzangu tuna darasa. Ni darasa ___.

misconceptions.cause: The child has not linked -angu, -ako, -ake, -etu, -enu, -ao to who owns the thing.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mimi na wenzangu tuna darasa. Ni darasa ___." with "langu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold up an object: Ni cha nani? Answer with the owner first, then the possessive.
misconceptions.feedback: Mwenye kitu ni nani? Mimi: changu; yeye: chake; wao: chao. (letu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the possessive before the noun (yangu kalamu), in English word order.
misconceptions.cause: English puts "my" before the noun; Kiswahili puts it after.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "yangu kalamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Build the phrase with cards: the noun first, then the possessive.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino kwanza, kimilikishi baadaye: kalamu yangu. (kalamu yangu)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kushiriki katika kutambua sauti lengwa katika kadi maneno,
kusikiliza matamshi ya sauti lengwa kutoka kwa mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali,
kutamka sauti lengwa akiwa na mwalimu kisha akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusikiliza silabi za sauti lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kutoka kwa vifaa vya kidijitali k.v. kinasasauti na rununu,
kutamka silabi alizozisikiliza ipasavyo akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutamka ipasavyo maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,
key_inquiry_questions: Ni sauti zipi unazojua kutamka?

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kutambua na kutamka sauti lengwa.

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/ in syllables and words (sikio, bega, damu), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The sounds of Theme 4 come first.
Naming body parts in Kiswahili.

misconceptions.error: Says /t/ for /d/, so "damu" becomes "tamu".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "damu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /d/, or do not separate it from /t/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "damu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "tamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "damu" ina sauti /d/, si /t/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /s/ for /z/, so "ziwa" becomes "siwa".
misconceptions.cause: /z/ and /s/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "siwa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: "ziwa" ina sauti /z/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "sikio" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "sikio" lina silabi zipi?" with "s-i-k-i-o" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: si-ki-o.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/g/ as "ji"), so the syllable cannot be built.
misconceptions.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "g" ni ipi?" with "ji" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the sound alone, short (/g/), then join it to a vowel: ga, ge, gi.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili tunatamka sauti: /g/.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/?" with "mkono" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "bega" ina sauti lengwa; "mkono" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Kusoma kwa Ufasaha Sauti: (/s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/) (Theme 6: Mwili wangu)

kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye maneno yenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatiakiwango kifaacho cha sauti akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha hadithi chenye maneno yenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 20 kwa dakika na kuzingatia viakifishi) akishirikiana na wenzake,

kuzingatia matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na kwa sauti inayosikika,

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 20 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying s, b, y, z, g, d comes before reading them.
Reading aloud with the sounds of Theme 4.

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "damu" as "tamu".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "damu" linasomwa vipi?" with "tamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "damu" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Baba ana sikio na bega."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Baba ana sikio na bega."?" with "Baba ... ana ... sikio ... na ... bega." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 20 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, goti lako linauma?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, goti lako linauma?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

outcomes.text: kutambua maneno yasiyozidi silabi tatu kutokana na suala lengwa

skills.name: Andika maneno yanayotamkwa kwenye imla kwa tahajia sahihi
skills.mastery: Writes the words the teacher reads (about 5 words) with the right letters: the Kiswahili sound and not the home sound, the nasal kept (nd, mb, ng), long vowels doubled and ng' with its apostrophe, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Joining syllables into words comes before writing them from dictation.
Hearing d and t, s and z clearly.

misconceptions.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "damu" written "tamu".
misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "tamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika "damu" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops the nasal: "ndevu" written "devu".
misconceptions.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "devu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
misconceptions.feedback: "ndevu" lina sauti ya pua mwanzoni.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "kaa" written "ka".
misconceptions.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "kuketi"." with "ka" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
misconceptions.feedback: "kaa" lina irabu mbili zinazofuatana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

misconceptions.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
misconceptions.feedback: Ng'ombe huandikwa na kibainishi: ng'.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
misconceptions.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the words aloud with a finger for each before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: "Kwa sababu" ni maneno mawili.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya - zuri na – baya (Theme 6: Mwili wangu)
learning_experiences: kutambua matumizi ya -zuri na -baya kwa kurejelea vitu katika mazingira yake,

kusoma sentensi zinazotumia maneno - zuri na -baya,

kujaza mapengo kwa kutumia - zuri na -baya,
kumtajia mzazi au mlezi vitu nyumbani kwa kutumia -zuri na - baya.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni maneno gani unayotumia kuelezea vitu vinavyokupendeza au visivyokupendeza?
sub_strands.core_competences:

Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kusikiliza matumizi ya-zuri na -baya.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapotumia -zuri na -baya.
Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapotumia -zuri na -baya.
sub_strands.values:

outcomes.text: kutambua matumizi ya-zuri na-baya katika kifungu
kutumia -zuri na - baya katika sentensi ili kuimarisha mawasiliano
kufurahia kutumia -zuri na -baya katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Tumia -zuri na -baya ipasavyo katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Uses -zuri and -baya after the noun with the right prefix (mtoto mzuri, kitabu kizuri, nguo nzuri, meno mabaya) and picks the one that matches the picture, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The ngeli and plural of nouns come before adjective agreement.
The m-mi and li-ma plurals (meno, mikono).

misconceptions.error: Gives the adjective the people prefix whatever the noun (kiti mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: Mzuri is the form the child hears most (mtoto mzuri) and is used everywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kitabu ___ (-zuri)." with "mzuri" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Match noun and adjective by colour: kiti kizuri, mtoto mzuri, vitu vizuri.
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi hufuata ngeli: kiti kizuri. (kizuri)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an n-n noun the m- form of the adjective (nyumba mzuri for nyumba nzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The n- prefix and its sound changes (nzuri, ndefu, nyeupe) are new to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Nguo ___ (-zuri)." with "mzuri" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read pairs aloud: nyumba nzuri, kalamu ndefu, nguo nyeupe.
misconceptions.feedback: Nyumba nzuri; nguo nyeupe. (nzuri)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the adjective before the noun (mzuri mtoto), in English word order.
misconceptions.cause: English puts the describing word first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "mzuri mtoto" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Build with cards: noun first, then the adjective.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino kwanza: mtoto mzuri. (mtoto mzuri)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the adjective singular with a plural noun (watoto mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun only.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Watoto ___ (-zuri)." with "mzuri" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change the noun to many and ask the child to change every word that goes with it.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto wazuri: vyote hubadilika. (wazuri)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks the opposite member of the pair (mrefu for a short person).

example.question: Picha inaonyesha meno machafu yenye mashimo. Meno ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The pair is learnt together and the two words are swapped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha meno machafu yenye mashimo. Meno ni ___." with "mazuri" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act the pairs with the body: stretch for refu, crouch for fupi.
misconceptions.feedback: Angalia picha tena na uchague neno linalofaa. (mabaya)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua maagizo kwa kutazama video ya maagizo,
kutoa na kufuata maagizo (kama vile simama, keti, andika na chora) akiwa na wenzake katika kikundi,
kueleza kuhusu maagizo yafaayo na yasiyofaa kufuatwa,
kushiriki katika mazungumzo ya matokeo ya kufuata na kutofuata maagizo,
kuimba na kuigiza nyimbo zinazohusu maagizo.
key_inquiry_questions: Ni maagizo yapi yanayotakiwa kufuatwa na yasiyotakiwa kufuatwa katika mazingira tofauti?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki kikamilifu katika kutoa na kuitikia maagizo ipasavyo.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia kifaa cha kidijitali kujifunzia maagizo.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapojifunza maagizo yanayotumiwa katika jamii yake.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapotambua na kufuata maagizo yafaayo.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapofuata maagizo na kuheshimu nafasi za wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi.
Uadilifu: mwanafunzi anapotoa na kufuata maagizo yafaayo.
sub_strands.pcis: Afya na usafi: mwanafunzi anapotoa au kufuata maagizo kuhusu suala lengwa.

outcomes.text: kutambua maagizo mepesi yanayotolewa darasani
kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi yanayotumiwa darasani
kubainisha maagizo yanayopaswa kufuatwa katika mazingira yake
kuthamini umuhimu wa maagizo katika maisha ya kila siku

skills.name: Fuata na utoe maagizo mepesi kwa usahihi
skills.mastery: Follows a one- or two-step instruction in the right order, reads the direction and action words in it (simama, keti, kulia, kushoto, juu, chini), and gives a clear, polite instruction that names what to do and to what, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Following a one-step instruction in pre-primary comes first.
A polite instruction uses tafadhali.

misconceptions.error: Carries out only the first part of a two-step instruction.

example.question: Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha uikaushe." Umefanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child starts acting as soon as he hears the first verb and stops listening.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha uikaushe." Umefanya nini?" with "anaosha mikono tu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold up one finger for each step while giving the instruction; the child repeats the steps before moving.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza agizo lote kwanza, kisha fanya hatua zote.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does the steps in the wrong order.

example.question: Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha ule chakula." Ni nini kinatangulia?

misconceptions.cause: The child does the step he wants most first; the order words kwanza and kisha are not yet noticed.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha ule chakula." Ni nini kinatangulia?" with "kula chakula" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Number the steps on the board with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
misconceptions.feedback: Neno "kisha" linaonyesha hatua inayofuata.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes a direction or action word.

example.question: Agizo: "Inua mkono wa kulia." Ni kitendo kipi sahihi?

misconceptions.cause: Pairs such as kulia/kushoto and juu/chini are learnt together and swapped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Inua mkono wa kulia." Ni kitendo kipi sahihi?" with "anainua mkono wa kushoto" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Play "Mwalimu anasema": the teacher calls the word, the child acts it; mark the right hand with a band.
misconceptions.feedback: Inua mkono wa kulia. maana yake ni anainua mkono wa kulia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an instruction that leaves out what to act on, or with no polite word (Lete!).

example.question: Ni agizo lipi liko wazi na lina adabu?

misconceptions.cause: The child knows what he means and does not see that the listener cannot.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni agizo lipi liko wazi na lina adabu?" with "Lete!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: The child gives the instruction to a partner, who does exactly what was said and no more.
misconceptions.feedback: Agizo zuri linasema nini kifanyike, kwa kitu gani, na kwa adabu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Kusoma kwa Ufahamu (Theme 7: Usafi wa mwili)
learning_experiences: kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 17-22- kuhusu suala lengwa na kutambua msamiati wa suala
lengwa (mimi, wenzangu) akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa (k.v. mimi, wenzangu, oga, nawa osha, maji, sabuni) kutoka kwenye kadi maneno, chati,
mti maneno, kapu maneno akishirikiana na wenzake,
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano,
kumweleza mzazi au mlezi kuhusu ujumbe aliopata kutokana na kifungu alichosoma. akishirikiana na wenzake,
key_inquiry_questions: Je, unapenda kusoma kuhusu nini?
sub_strands.design_notes: Second read left this for a person to confirm: competencies: not in the design; values: not in the design; pcis: not in the design; links: not in the design.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kutabiri yatayotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu kwa kuzingatia picha
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kuchangamkia kusoma vifungu vya ufahamu ili kuimarisha stadi ya kusoma

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on usafi wa mwili, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues in the picture and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The vocabulary and message of a short passage (Theme 5) come first.
Saying what is happening in a picture is the base for predicting from it.

misconceptions.error: Gives "husugua" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Kila asubuhi Baraka huoga kwa maji na sabuni. Yeye husugua meno na kuchana nywele. Baraka huwa safi." Neno "husugua" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Kila asubuhi Baraka huoga kwa maji na sabuni. Yeye husugua meno na kuchana nywele. Baraka huwa safi." Neno "husugua" lina maana gani?" with "husahau" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "husugua" ni husafisha kwa kusugua.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Tuoge na kusafisha mwili kila siku.

misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Baraka huchana nywele." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tuoge na kusafisha mwili kila siku.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for, without looking at the picture.

example.question: Picha inaonyesha mikono michafu ya Baraka kabla ya chakula. Atafanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha mikono michafu ya Baraka kabla ya chakula. Atafanya nini?" with "Atakula moja kwa moja." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words and point at the picture; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za picha na za kifungu: Ataosha mikono kwa sabuni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.
misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Baraka huoga asubuhi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tunapaswa kuweka miili yetu safi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Baraka huoga kwa nini?" with "Mimi huoga kwa maji moto." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: maji na sabuni
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Andika maneno kwa tahajia sahihi
skills.mastery: Writes the words of his own writing (about 5 words) with the right letters: the Kiswahili sound and not the home sound, the nasal kept (nd, mb, ng), long vowels doubled and ng' with its apostrophe, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Writing words from dictation (Theme 6) comes first.
Joining syllables into a word.

misconceptions.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "taulo" written "tauro".
misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "tauro" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika "taulo" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops the nasal: "ndoo" written "doo".
misconceptions.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "doo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
misconceptions.feedback: "ndoo" lina sauti ya pua mwanzoni.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "choo" written "cho".

example.question: Andika neno lenye maana ya "chumba cha kujisaidia".

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "chumba cha kujisaidia"." with "cho" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
misconceptions.feedback: "choo" lina irabu mbili zinazofuatana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

misconceptions.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
misconceptions.feedback: Ng'ombe huandikwa na kibainishi: ng'.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
misconceptions.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the words aloud with a finger for each before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: "Kwa sababu" ni maneno mawili.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher
