skills.name: Kanusha sentensi za nafsi ya kwanza umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Makes the negative of a present-tense sentence in the first person: mimi ninaoga - mimi siogi, sisi tunaoga - sisi hatuogi (si-/hatu-, no -na-, final -a to -i), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Mimi/sisi and their subject markers (Theme 1) come before their negatives.
Instructions of the same theme use the same verbs (osha, chana).

misconceptions.error: Keeps the final -a in the negative present (hasoma for hasomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child adds the negative prefix and leaves the rest of the verb as it was.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Mimi ninaoga." with "Mimi sioga." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show the pair with the end of the verb circled: anasoma - hasomi.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika ukanushaji wa wakati uliopo, -a inakuwa -i: hasomi. (Mimi siogi.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps the tense marker -na- in the negative (hanasomi for hasomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child negates by adding ha- to the whole positive verb.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Mimi ninaosha mikono." with "Mimi sinaoshi mikono." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cross out na in the positive form and change the end.
misconceptions.feedback: Hasomi: hakuna -na- katika ukanushaji huu. (Mimi sioshi mikono.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Negates by putting si before the positive verb (Yeye si anasoma).
misconceptions.cause: Si is the negative the child knows (si mimi), so he puts it in front of any sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Sisi tunachana nywele." with "Sisi si tunachana nywele." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show si as the negative of ni (Yeye si mwalimu) and ha- as the negative of a verb.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendo hukanushwa kwa ha-: Yeye hasomi. (Sisi hatuchani nywele.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the negative prefix of another person (Wao hasomi for hawasomi; Mimi hasomi for sisomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child learnt one negative form (ha-) and uses it for all persons.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Sisi tunasugua meno." with "Sisi hasugui meno." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Table of persons: si-, hu-, ha-, hatu-, ham-, hawa-; the child points before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Wao hawasomi; mimi sisomi. (Sisi hatusugui meno.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/ in syllables and words (viazi, papai, shamba), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The sounds of Theme 6 come first.
Naming foods in Kiswahili.

misconceptions.error: Says /f/ for /v/, so "viazi" becomes "fiazi".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "viazi". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /v/, or do not separate it from /f/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "viazi". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "fiazi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "viazi" ina sauti /v/, si /f/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /s/ for /sh/, so "shamba" becomes "samba".
misconceptions.cause: /sh/ and /s/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "samba" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: "shamba" ina sauti /sh/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "viazi" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "viazi" lina silabi zipi?" with "v-i-a-z-i" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: vi-a-zi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/j/ as "jei"), so the syllable cannot be built.
misconceptions.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "j" ni ipi?" with "jei" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the sound alone, short (/j/), then join it to a vowel: ja, je, ji.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili tunatamka sauti: /j/.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/?" with "ugali" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "papai" ina sauti lengwa; "ugali" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /j/, /r/, /p/, /f/, /v/, /sh/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 25 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying j, r, p, f, v, sh comes before reading them.
Reading aloud with the sounds of Theme 6.

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "viazi" as "fiazi".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "viazi" linasomwa vipi?" with "fiazi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "viazi" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Tunakula viazi na papai."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Tunakula viazi na papai."?" with "Tunakula ... viazi ... na ... papai." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 25 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, umekunywa uji?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, umekunywa uji?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.core_competences:

Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapotunga na kuandika sentensi akizingatia tahajia sahihi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoweza kutunga sententensi sahihi.
sub_strands.values:

skills.name: Andika insha fupi kwa tahajia sahihi za maneno
skills.mastery: Writes the words of his own writing (about 10 words) with the right letters: the Kiswahili sound and not the home sound, the nasal kept (nd, mb, ng), long vowels doubled and ng' with its apostrophe, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Spelling single words comes before spelling in three sentences.
Each of the three sentences ends with a kikomo.

misconceptions.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "mchele" written "mchere".
misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "mchere" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika "mchele" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops the nasal: "ndizi" written "dizi".
misconceptions.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "dizi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
misconceptions.feedback: "ndizi" lina sauti ya pua mwanzoni.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "mkaa" written "mka".

example.question: Andika neno lenye maana ya "kitu kinachochomwa kupikia".

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "kitu kinachochomwa kupikia"." with "mka" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
misconceptions.feedback: "mkaa" lina irabu mbili zinazofuatana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

misconceptions.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
misconceptions.feedback: Ng'ombe huandikwa na kibainishi: ng'.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
misconceptions.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the words aloud with a finger for each before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: "Kwa sababu" ni maneno mawili.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya hiki na hivi (Theme 8: Vyakula vyetu)

sub_strands.core_competences:

skills.name: Tumia hiki na hivi kuonyeshea vitu
skills.mastery: Points at one ki-vi thing near him with hiki and at many with hivi (chakula hiki - vyakula hivi, kiazi hiki - viazi hivi), not huyu or hii, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Huyu and hawa (Theme 3) are the first pointing words.
The ki-vi plural (kiti - viti) from Theme 2.

misconceptions.error: Uses the people word (huyu, yule) for a thing (kiti huyu).
misconceptions.cause: Huyu was the first pointing word learnt; the child uses it for anything.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Chakula ___ ni kitamu." with "huyu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Point at a child (huyu) and at a chair (hiki); then sort pictures by the pointing word they take.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitu cha ngeli ya ki-vi huonyeshwa kwa hiki; mtu huonyeshwa kwa huyu. (hiki)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the one-thing pointing word with a plural noun (watoto huyu).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun but not the pointing word.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Vyakula ___ ni vitamu." with "hiki" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair the forms on cards: huyu-hawa, yule-wale, hiki-hivi, hili-haya.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto ni wengi: watoto hawa. (hivi)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses hii for every noun (kitabu hii, mtoto hii), as in town Kiswahili.
misconceptions.cause: Hii is the pointing word heard most in town speech, where the noun class is dropped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kikombe ___ ni changu." with "hii" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read pairs aloud: kitabu hiki, mtoto huyu, nyumba hii; the child hears the match.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitabu hiki; mtoto huyu; nyumba hii. (hiki)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).
misconceptions.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kipi ni umoja?" with "viazi hivi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (kiazi hiki)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Shiriki mazungumzo kuhusu vyombo vya jikoni kwa zamu, kwa matamshi bora na ishara zifaazo
skills.mastery: Takes part in a short conversation about vyombo vya jikoni: keeps to the topic, waits for his turn, speaks Kiswahili without English or Sheng words, says sounds clearly and uses gestures that match the words, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Talking about a picture in pre-primary comes before a short conversation.
Listening for what others say is half of a conversation.

misconceptions.error: Says something that has nothing to do with the topic.

example.question: Mnazungumza kuhusu vyombo vya jikoni. Ni sentensi ipi inafaa?

misconceptions.cause: The child says what is on his mind; he has not learnt that a conversation has a topic everyone keeps to.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mnazungumza kuhusu vyombo vya jikoni. Ni sentensi ipi inafaa?" with "Jana nilitazama katuni nzuri." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Put the topic picture in the middle; before speaking the child points to it.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunazungumza kuhusu vyombo vya jikoni; sema jambo kuhusu hilo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Talks over others and does not wait for his turn.
misconceptions.cause: Eagerness: the child fears he will forget his idea.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwenzako anazungumza. Unafanya nini?" with "ninaanza kuzungumza pia" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pass a talking object (a ball): only the one holding it speaks.
misconceptions.feedback: Subiri zamu yako; msikilize mwenzako kwanza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili sentence.
misconceptions.cause: At home and in town the child hears mixed speech and does not know the Kiswahili word.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sema kwa Kiswahili sanifu:" with "Mama ana fridge jikoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word wall: the English or Sheng word, and its Kiswahili word next to it.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili tunasema: Mama ana jokofu jikoni.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses a gesture or face that does not match the words (smiling while giving sad news).

example.question: Unasema "Rafiki yangu ni mgonjwa." Uso wako unaonyesha nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child smiles from shyness or does not link the face to the message.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unasema "Rafiki yangu ni mgonjwa." Uso wako unaonyesha nini?" with "tabasamu kubwa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say one sentence with three faces; the class picks the face that fits.
misconceptions.feedback: Ishara zako zifuate ujumbe wako.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /l/ for /r/ (or /r/ for /l/) while speaking: "rafiki" becomes "lafiki".
misconceptions.cause: Several Kenyan first languages do not separate /l/ and /r/; the home sound carries into Kiswahili.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tamka vizuri: rafiki" with "lafiki" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Practise the pairs with a mirror: the tongue taps for r, it rests for l.
misconceptions.feedback: Tamka "rafiki" kwa /r/: ulimi unagonga mara moja.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

key_inquiry_questions: Je, tunaweza kujifunza mambo yapi kutokana na hadithi mbalimbali?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi na kuchangia kikamilifu kutambua ujumbe katika kifungu.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali katika shughuli za ujifunzaji.

Uwazaji kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapotabiri matukio ya hadithi kwa kutazama picha.
sub_strands.values:
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kujadiliana.

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on jikoni, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues in the picture and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The four comprehension questions of Theme 7 come first.
Reading the passage aloud.

misconceptions.error: Gives "sufuria" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Mama yuko jikoni. Anapika ugali na sukumawiki. Dada anaosha sufuria. Chakula kiko tayari." Neno "sufuria" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Mama yuko jikoni. Anapika ugali na sukumawiki. Dada anaosha sufuria. Chakula kiko tayari." Neno "sufuria" lina maana gani?" with "sufu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "sufuria" ni chombo cha kupikia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.
misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Dada anaosha sufuria." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Familia hushirikiana kupika chakula.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for, without looking at the picture.

example.question: Picha inaonyesha meza yenye sahani. Familia itafanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha meza yenye sahani. Familia itafanya nini?" with "Italala." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words and point at the picture; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za picha na za kifungu: Itakula chakula pamoja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.

example.question: Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?
example.correct_answer: Tunapaswa kuwasaidia wazazi kazi za jikoni.

misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Mama anapika ugali." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tunapaswa kuwasaidia wazazi kazi za jikoni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mama anapika nini?" with "Mama yangu anapika wali." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: ugali na sukumawiki
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Andika kifungu kifupi kutokana na picha
skills.mastery: Writes a short paragraph about a picture on jikoni: a title that fits, sentences in order, one tense, Kiswahili words only, capitals and kikomo in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying what is happening in a picture comes before writing it.
Writing three short sentences with correct spelling (Theme 8).

misconceptions.error: Lists the things in the picture (mti, mtoto, mbwa) instead of writing sentences about what is happening.

example.question: Ni kipi ni kifungu kuhusu picha?
example.correct_answer: Mtoto anacheza na mbwa chini ya mti.

misconceptions.cause: Naming pictures was the earlier task; the child has not moved to sentences.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kipi ni kifungu kuhusu picha?" with "mti. mtoto. mbwa." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask "Nani? Anafanya nini? Wapi?" for each part of the picture.
misconceptions.feedback: Kifungu kina sentensi zinazoeleza kinachotokea.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes no title, or a title that does not fit the writing.

example.question: Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu jikoni?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the word "insha" or the date is the title.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu jikoni?" with "Insha" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the finished writing and ask: what is it about in three words?
misconceptions.feedback: Kichwa kinasema insha inahusu nini: Jikoni Kwetu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins every sentence with "na halafu", so the writing is one long sentence.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni.
example.correct_answer: Tuliamka asubuhi. Tulioga, kisha tukaenda sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: Spoken retelling joins events with na halafu; the child writes as he talks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a word bank: kwanza, kisha, baadaye, mwishowe; one per sentence.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia kikomo na maneno kama kisha, baadaye.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Slips from one tense to another in the middle of the writing (past -li- to present -na-, or habitual hu- to past).

example.question: Ni lipi sahihi?
example.wrong_answer: Mama alipika ugali. Dada anaosha vyombo.
example.correct_answer: Mama alipika ugali. Dada aliosha vyombo.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks of the events as he writes and the tense of the moment comes in.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mama alipika ugali. Dada anaosha vyombo." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline every verb; all the tense markers should match.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia wakati mmoja katika insha nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili writing.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not know the Kiswahili word and fills the gap with the one he knows.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sahihisha:" with "Mama anapika rice." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word bank of theme words on the board before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili: Mama anapika wali.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Matumizi ya Maneno Yanayoashiria Vitendo (Theme 9: Jikoni)
learning_experiences: kutambua maneno yanayoashiria vitendo katika kadi maneno, mti maneno, chati au vifaa vya kidijitali,
kutaja mambo aliyofanya siku hiyo kama vile, kula, kuvaa, kupika, kuwasha, kuosha, pakua,
kuigiza vitendo k.m. kula, kunywa, keti, simama, nawa, choma,
kusoma maneno yanayoashiria vitendo ili kujenga usomaji bora,
kukamilisha sentensi akitumia maneno yanayoashiria vitendo,
kutunga sentensi zenye matumizi ya maneno yanayoashiria vitendo,
kumtungia mwenzake katika kikundi sentensi kwa kutumia maneno yanayoashiria vitendo,
kufanya zoezi la kujaza nafasi katika madaftari yao.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni mambo yapi uliyofanya tangu jana?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika utunzi wa sentensi na wenzake katika kikundi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapotungia mwenzake sentensi kwa kutumia maneno yanayoashiria vitendo.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapofanya zoezi akitumia kifaa cha kidijitali.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi sahihi akitumia maneno yanayoashiria vitendo.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu mchango wa wenzake katika shughuli za kikundi wanapotungiana sentensi kwa kutumia maneno yanayoashiria vitendo.
Haki za kijamii: mwanafunzi anapoigiza vitendo akiwa na mwenzake huku akizingatia maslahi ya mwenzake k.v. ikiwa mwenzake ana mahitaji maalumu.
sub_strands.pcis:
Uraia: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi.
Matumizi ya pesa: mwanafunzi anapojifunza vitendo k.v. nunua.

skills.name: Tambua na utumie maneno yanayoashiria vitendo
skills.mastery: Finds the action word in a short sentence (Mama anapika ugali: anapika), reads it, and uses an action word with the right person marker (mama anapika, watoto wanakula), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The person marker on the verb (Theme 1) is part of every action word.
Instructions are action words the child already follows.

misconceptions.error: Picks a thing word as the action word (in "Mama anapika ugali" chooses ugali).

example.question: Neno la kitendo katika "Mama anapika ugali" ni lipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child looks for the word he knows best, often the thing he can picture.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno la kitendo katika "Mama anapika ugali" ni lipi?" with "ugali" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act the sentence: the word you can do is the action word.
misconceptions.feedback: Neno la kitendo ni lile tunaloweza kulifanya: anapika. (anapika)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes the bare verb with no person marker (Mama pika ugali for Mama anapika ugali).
misconceptions.cause: The command form (pika!) is heard most at home and the child uses it in every sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mama pika ugali." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Colour the a-na- in front of the verb; read the sentence with and without it.
misconceptions.feedback: Tunasema "Mama anapika", si "Mama pika". (Mama anapika ugali.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives the verb the marker of the wrong person or number (Mama wanapika; Watoto anacheza).
misconceptions.cause: The child has not linked the start of the verb to who is doing it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Watoto ___ (kula) chakula." with "anakula" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Point at the doer, then at the start of the verb; they must match (mmoja a-, wengi wa-).
misconceptions.feedback: Mtu mmoja: anapika; watu wengi: wanapika. (wanakula)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes a describing word for an action word (in "Sahani ni safi" chooses safi as the action).

example.question: Neno la kitendo katika "Dada anaosha sahani safi" ni lipi?

misconceptions.cause: Any word after the noun looks like what the noun "does".
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno la kitendo katika "Dada anaosha sahani safi" ni lipi?" with "safi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask "Inafanya nini?" If there is no answer, there is no action word.
misconceptions.feedback: Neno la kitendo linaonyesha kinachofanywa, kama "anaosha". (anaosha)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /ny/, /dh/, /th/, /ch/, /gh/, /ng/, /ng'/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /ny/, /dh/, /th/, /ch/, /gh/, /ng/, /ng'/ in syllables and words (ngoma, chenga, nyota), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The single sounds of Themes 2 to 8 come before the two-letter sounds.
Hearing and repeating a sound.

misconceptions.error: Says /z/ for /dh/, so "dhahabu" becomes "zahabu".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "dhahabu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /dh/, or do not separate it from /z/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "dhahabu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "zahabu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "dhahabu" ina sauti /dh/, si /z/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Says /sh/ for /ch/, so "chenga" becomes "shenga".
misconceptions.cause: /ch/ and /sh/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "shenga" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: "chenga" ina sauti /ch/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops part of the target sound, so "ngoma" becomes "goma".

example.question: Neno "ngoma" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?

misconceptions.cause: The second part of the sound (the w or y glide, or the soft nasal) is quick and quiet; the child does not hear it and leaves it out.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "ngoma" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?" with "goma" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stretch the syllable slowly (p-y-a), then say it fast; the child copies.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza tena: "ngoma". Usiache sehemu ya sauti.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "ngoma" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "ngoma" lina silabi zipi?" with "n-g-o-m-a" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: ngo-ma.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /ny/, /dh/, /th/, /ch/, /gh/, /ng/, /ng'/?" with "mpira" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "chenga" ina sauti lengwa; "mpira" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /ny/, /dh/, /th/, /ch/, /gh/, /ng/, /ng'/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /ny/, /dh/, /th/, /ch/, /gh/, /ng/, /ng'/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 30 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying the two-letter sounds comes before reading them.
Reading aloud with the sounds of Theme 8.

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "chenga" as "shenga".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "chenga" linasomwa vipi?" with "shenga" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "chenga" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Tunacheza ngoma uwanjani."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Tunacheza ngoma uwanjani."?" with "Tunacheza ... ngoma ... uwanjani." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 30 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, umeona nyota?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, umeona nyota?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Andika kifungu kifupi kutokana na picha
skills.mastery: Writes a short paragraph about a picture on michezo: a title that fits, sentences in order, one tense, Kiswahili words only, capitals and kikomo in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: A paragraph from a picture (Theme 9) comes first.
Talking about a picture.

misconceptions.error: Lists the things in the picture (mti, mtoto, mbwa) instead of writing sentences about what is happening.

example.question: Ni kipi ni kifungu kuhusu picha?
example.correct_answer: Mtoto anacheza na mbwa chini ya mti.

misconceptions.cause: Naming pictures was the earlier task; the child has not moved to sentences.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni kipi ni kifungu kuhusu picha?" with "mti. mtoto. mbwa." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask "Nani? Anafanya nini? Wapi?" for each part of the picture.
misconceptions.feedback: Kifungu kina sentensi zinazoeleza kinachotokea.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes no title, or a title that does not fit the writing.

example.question: Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu michezo?

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks the word "insha" or the date is the title.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kichwa kipi kinafaa insha kuhusu michezo?" with "Insha" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the finished writing and ask: what is it about in three words?
misconceptions.feedback: Kichwa kinasema insha inahusu nini: Michezo Shuleni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins every sentence with "na halafu", so the writing is one long sentence.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni.
example.correct_answer: Tuliamka asubuhi. Tulioga, kisha tukaenda sokoni.

misconceptions.cause: Spoken retelling joins events with na halafu; the child writes as he talks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Tuliamka na halafu tukaoga na halafu tukaenda sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a word bank: kwanza, kisha, baadaye, mwishowe; one per sentence.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia kikomo na maneno kama kisha, baadaye.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Slips from one tense to another in the middle of the writing (past -li- to present -na-, or habitual hu- to past).

example.question: Ni lipi sahihi?
example.wrong_answer: Jana tulicheza mpira. Juma anafunga bao.
example.correct_answer: Jana tulicheza mpira. Juma alifunga bao.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks of the events as he writes and the tense of the moment comes in.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Jana tulicheza mpira. Juma anafunga bao." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline every verb; all the tense markers should match.
misconceptions.feedback: Tumia wakati mmoja katika insha nzima.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts English or Sheng words into the Kiswahili writing.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not know the Kiswahili word and fills the gap with the one he knows.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sahihisha:" with "Tulicheza football." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a word bank of theme words on the board before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Kwa Kiswahili: Tulicheza mpira wa miguu.
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utumie vinyume vya vitendo
skills.mastery: Gives the opposite action of a simple verb (anza - maliza, keti - simama, ingia - toka, panda - shuka), not its negative, a word of the same meaning or a place word, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Finding action words (Theme 9) comes before their opposites.
Knowing the negative lets the child tell it from the opposite.

misconceptions.error: Gives the negative of the verb (hafungui) instead of its opposite action (funga).
misconceptions.cause: The child thinks "opposite" means "not doing it".
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "anza" (mchezo) ni?" with "usianze" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act it: fungua the door, then funga it; not doing anything is not the opposite.
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha kitendo ni kitendo kingine: fungua - funga. (maliza)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes an opposite by adding -ua to any verb (keti -> ketua).
misconceptions.cause: Fungua/funga and vaa/vua show a pattern, and the child uses it everywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "keti" ni?" with "ketua" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort pairs into two piles: made with -ua (funga-fungua) and different words (keti-simama).
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha keti ni simama. (simama)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a word of the same meaning as the opposite (simama - inuka).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows the words go together but not that they mean the same.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "ingia" ni?" with "jiunga" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act both words: if the action is the same, it is not the opposite.
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume ni kitendo kinachopingana. (toka)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a place or thing word as the opposite of an action (ingia - nje).
misconceptions.cause: Ingia and nje are heard together in "ingia ndani, toka nje".
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kinyume cha "panda" (mti) ni?" with "chini" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask "Ni kitendo?" before accepting: the opposite of an action is an action.
misconceptions.feedback: Kinyume cha ingia ni toka. (shuka)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

readiness.name: Hear and repeat sounds and short words
readiness.what: Listens to a sound, a rhyme or a short word said by the teacher and says it back clearly.

readiness.name: Hear and say the five vowel sounds
readiness.what: Says a, e, i, o, u as Kiswahili sounds and picks the one heard at the start of a familiar word.

readiness.name: Name everyday things and people in Kiswahili
readiness.what: Names common objects, body parts, family members and foods at home and in class in Kiswahili.

readiness.name: Greet and answer at home and in class
readiness.what: Greets a parent, a teacher and a friend and answers a greeting, in Kiswahili or the home language.

readiness.name: Follow a one-step spoken instruction
readiness.what: Does what a short spoken instruction asks (simama, keti, lete kitabu).

readiness.name: Talk about a picture and handle a book
readiness.what: Holds a picture book the right way up, turns pages one at a time and says what is happening in a picture.

readiness.name: Answer who and what about a story heard
readiness.what: After listening to a short story, says who was in it and one thing that happened.

readiness.name: Hold a crayon and draw pre-writing patterns
readiness.what: Holds a crayon or pencil between thumb and fingers and draws lines, curves and circles from left to right.
